title: Khalsa Sovereignty and the London Record

blocks.text: This prefatory page insists that Khalsa sovereignty is real and divinely grounded, not a fiction invented by admirers or enemies. The narrator frames the coming history as a truthful defense of Sikh authority and warns that hostile accounts have obscured what the Panth actually became.

The argument also turns outward toward imperial readers, repeating that the matter should be written carefully and sent onward as a reliable record. References to London and royal inquiry show that the book imagines Sikh history being judged far beyond Punjab itself.

As a result, the page functions as the last argumentative bridge before the formal opening. It closes the defense of Sikh legitimacy and prepares the reader for the invocation and first episode that follow.
